tldr: Headlines across all 12 country buckets foreground the Witkoff-Kushner shuttle between Moscow and Kyiv as a historic US diplomatic push to end the Ukraine war, with Russia's conditional openness to resumed talks treated as the lead development; only three outlets surface the Russian missile strikes that continued through and after the envoys' visit.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to explicitly flag 'No Sign of Breakthrough' — uniquely skeptical framing that contrasts with the Kremlin's own 'useful' language (RT/Meduza) and the broadly optimistic peace-push framing seen everywhere else.

Only outlet to foreground 'atmosphere of trust' between US and Russia — framing the talks as US-Russia bilateral rapprochement rather than a Ukraine peace process, invisible in every other title worldwide.
Only headline leading with civilian casualties from Russian strikes ('kill 2') rather than any diplomatic activity — the lone outlet whose front-page story is the war's violence, not the peace push.

bottom_line: The headline layer globally sells a single story: a US-brokered diplomatic push — Witkoff and Kushner's first-ever Kyiv visit headlining virtually every outlet — while the concurrent Russian missile strikes that killed civilians surface in only three titles and the absence of any formal peace plan is acknowledged only by Ukrainian and exiled-Russian outlets.
